findings.because: Working with masa and Pleating dumplings each carry their own written standard in the brief (standard: true, four marks each). findings.claim: proof by volume and the poke test and never by the clock, then fermentation, which is a rate, not a duration
findings.because: A loaf does not proof then ferment. Bulk fermentation comes after kneading and before shaping; proofing is the final rise before the oven (the brief's own Proofing definition: 'the final rise before baking'), and scoring follows proofing. The primer says 'the order the loaf does' and then gives the wrong order.
findings.fix: ferment, which is a rate, not a duration, then proof by volume and the poke test and never by the clock, then score

findings.claim: Scoring's standard is about the blade, not the loaf: one clean draw at a slant, parallel lines a finger's width apart, through the skin and no deeper than the fat.
findings.because: The app's Scoring standard is written for skin over fat, not bread: its marks say the cut 'parts through the skin and stops in the fat beneath', 'red or fibrous flesh has gone too deep', the surface should be 'dry and cold, near 4C', and the fault has the cuts 'bleed as they cook'. A loaf has no fat layer and no flesh, so 'no deeper than the fat' inside 'the order the loaf does' will read as nonsense to a baker and misdirect a cook scoring pork belly or duck.
findings.fix: Scoring's standard is written for skin over fat, not for a loaf: one clean draw at a slant on a cold dry surface, parallel lines a finger's width apart, through the skin and stopping in the fat, never the flesh.

critic.notes:
Placement worth the operator's eye, not a primer fault: five Level II dishes are built on techniques the data places at Level III. Jerk Chicken carries Jerk and Grilling over live coals; Huli Huli Chicken carries Grilling over live coals and Butchery basics; Memphis Dry-Rub Ribs carries Low & slow smoking; Whole Grilled Fish with Ladolemono carries Filleting fish and Grilling over live coals; Linguine alle Vongole carries Shucking shellfish. The 2-dishes primer tells the cook to grill over coals and fillet off the grill at Level II, and the 2-techniques next line then says those are Level III techniques. Either the Fire & Smoke dishes and the two fish plates belong a level up, or those techniques a level down. In the same vein the Floor Deck places Beurre Blanc and Meunière at Level III and Hollandaise at Level I, while the beurre blanc and hollandaise techniques and Sole Meunière sit at Level II; a reader meets the same word at two levels three times on this page (the deck fix above softens one of them).

The 2-safety primer cannot name its fourth item: rule 4 bans the word in its label, so the reader is told about "the protocol" and "the fourth entry" without learning which protocol. The primer is honest within the rule, but it is the one place on the level page where a cook is pointed at something unnamed. If the gate can allow an item's own label as a name in a safety primer, the primer should say it; otherwise this is the ceiling.

Tooling: the technique brief carries standard: true and not the marks, so the 2-techniques author had to reach technique-standards.json for the sentences it paraphrases (scoring on skin over fat, the water bath's 80 to 85 C, the tadka order), and the refuters could not have checked them against the brief. Putting each technique's marks and fault in the brief would let the data refuter do that check. Also, every brief carries the levelTest line, so five of eight authors closed on it; the brief could mark it as the level page's door to mention once per level, or the level page could carry it so no primer has to.

Verified against the briefs and the data with nothing further to fix: the eighteen dishes' minutes, semesters and techniques; the 21 of 50 techniques with a standard and the marks quoted; the 255 lexicon terms and every cited term's text; the 122 deck cards checked by name (ghee, clarified butter, demi-glace, morel, enoki, macaron, coppa, wagyu); the 16 plates and their corrections, and 20 plates on the wall; the two faults and their levers and the rung 2 note; the eight service modules and their outcomes and 27 on the track; the cooling law's figures and the four safety entries; all eight next lines against neighbours.above.
